findings.body: Active `/stop` and `/new` run before this path checks whether their admission item was already consumed. A recovery wake can route and consume the item through the live-turn router while an admission worker still holds its claim; `takeInput` permits claimed items. The admission worker can then execute the same command again, and the failed `consumeInputItem` call only logs after the side effect. Claim the item for control handling before executing the command, and cover this two-worker race.
findings.title: Not done: No message is lost or given twice

findings.body: This path treats a successful continuation-file write as delivery and marks the command applied. The unchanged `continuation-input.ts:65-84` only writes a file; it provides no confirmation that the runner read it before closing. Such a follow-up remains consumed without reaching the model or the next turn. The story assigns runner delivery confirmation and release of unconfirmed commands to T4.
findings.title: Later: T4 must confirm that the runner read a follow-up

findings.body: The router takes only the oldest item. If an active turn requires a particular continuation sender, `live-turn-routing.ts:50-56` rejects an item from another sender and this branch releases it. Every subsequent wake takes that same item again, preventing a later item from the required sender from reaching the waiting runner on a single admission worker. Defer the rejected item until the turn ends or examine later eligible items.
findings.title: Do not let a rejected follow-up block the required sender

findings.body: Ordinary turns pass `admissionAppId`, but the pre-command and compaction runs built in unchanged `group-session-command-runner.ts:39-53` omit it. This fallback selects `default` for a normal channel JID owned by a non-default app, so those runs can resolve provider configuration and agent session context in the wrong app.
findings.title: Pass the admission app ID to session-command agent runs

findings.body: This added task-status file contains prior review findings and status. It is outside the permitted paths, is not needed for the record switch or its tests, and the supplied handoff gives no reason for including it.
findings.title: Remove the unrelated review-state file outside scope
